title: SLO-driven regional evacuation and graceful degradation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an SLO-driven policy and implementation plan to progressively evacuate traffic from a degraded region while preserving overall platform SLOs. The feature will: 1) compute per-region real-time SLO risk (latency and availability), 2) attach circuit-breaker decisions to per-route policy graphs, 3) steer by latency+capacity hints with geo pinning exemptions, and 4) apply prioritized load-shedding and model fallback tiers during constrained conditions. This ticket covers design, prototype, rollout, and runbook for on-call remediation and automated evacuation flows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated regional evacuation can be triggered by an SLO breach detection signal (simulated) and will reduce traffic to the target region by >95% within the configured ramp window. 2) No user-visible error rate increase beyond allowable cross-region failover budget. 3) Circuit-breaker metrics (tripped_count, trip_duration) and route-level shedding events are emitted to observability with dashboards and alerts. 4) Canary rollout ends with successful rollback criteria and documented runbook for manual override.
tasks: Design policy DSL for SLO -> action mapping (latency thresholds, error budgets, ramp windows)
Implement SLO scorer service to synthesize p50/p95/p99 latency + error rate per region
Extend request director to accept dynamic capacity hints and per-request geo pins
Add circuit-breaker primitive with soft/hard thresholds and exponential backoff
Implement prioritized shedding backend (tiered customers, model-size fallback, retry-after headers)
End-to-end test harness that can simulate region latency spikes and capacity loss
Dashboard and alerting: SLO risk, evacuation progress, shedding counts, rollback triggers
Runbook and playbook for oncall to perform manual evacuation and reconcile incidents
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha in staging cluster w/ synthetic traffic (2 weeks). Phase 2: limited canary in us-east (5% traffic) with automated abort on increased p99 > baseline+40ms or error delta > 0.5%. Phase 3: ramp to 25% and coverage of tiered customers; monitor for 48h. Phase 4: global rollout with per-region defaults and opt-outs for pinned customers.
